current_activity: assembles just north of Le Muy as VI Corps' mobile striking force
notes: Event date: 17 August 1944, evening (Clarke and Smith, ch. 8). Event definition: By evening on 17 August almost all of the task force, a brigade-sized unit of a cavalry squadron, a tank battalion, a motorised infantry battalion, tank destroyers and armoured artillery, has assembled just north of Le Muy (Clarke and Smith, ch. 8). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 8, p. 132: "By evening on 17 August, almost all of TF Butler had assembled just north of Le Muy". Location: Le Muy, Var (PL0873) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Clarke and Smith say just north of Le Muy. Commander: Brigadier General Frederick B. Butler, VI Corps deputy commander (Clarke and Smith, ch. 5).

current_activity: reaches Sisteron on the Durance after the action at Digne; patrols west towards the Rhône
notes: Event date: 19 August 1944 (Clarke and Smith, chs. 8-9). Event definition: Striking north from Barjols on 18 August, the task force crosses the Verdon, helps the FFI take the German garrison of Digne and reaches Sisteron on 19 August, holding Durance bridges and patrolling west to within thirty miles of Avignon (Clarke and Smith, ch. 8). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 8, p. 134: "seize Sisteron (which TF Butler reached about four hours later)". Location: Sisteron, Alpes-de-Haute-Provence (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Clarke and Smith name Sisteron. Commander: Brigadier General Frederick B. Butler, VI Corps deputy commander (Clarke and Smith, ch. 5).

current_activity: regroups at Aspres and turns west for Montélimar on Truscott's orders
notes: Event date: 21 August 1944, daybreak (Clarke and Smith, ch. 9). Event definition: Ordered at 2045 on 20 August to move to Montélimar, the task force regroups at Aspres by daybreak on the 21st, leaves detachments at the Croix Haute pass and Gap, and starts the rest of the command west (Clarke and Smith, ch. 9). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 9, p. 147: "By daybreak of 21 August, Butler had regrouped the bulk of his task force at Aspres". Location: Aspres-sur-Buëch, Hautes-Alpes (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Clarke and Smith name Aspres. Commander: Brigadier General Frederick B. Butler, VI Corps deputy commander (Clarke and Smith, ch. 5).

current_activity: reaches the high ground north of Montélimar; command post at Marsanne by 2330
notes: Event date: 21 August 1944, late afternoon to 2330 (Clarke and Smith, ch. 9). Event definition: Late on 21 August the task force moves south from Crest to Marsanne in the centre of the battle square, probing towards La Coucourde, Sauzet and Montélimar; Butler sets up his command post at Marsanne and reports arrival at 2330 (Clarke and Smith, ch. 9). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 9, p. 149: "After establishing his command post at Marsanne, he sent a message to Truscott". Location: Marsanne, Drôme (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Clarke and Smith name Marsanne. Commander: Brigadier General Frederick B. Butler, VI Corps deputy commander (Clarke and Smith, ch. 5).

current_activity: under the 36th Division, attacks west from the Condillac Pass to restore the La Coucourde roadblock
notes: Event date: 26 August 1944 (Clarke and Smith, ch. 9). Event definition: After a night march the task force assembles in the Condillac Pass and attacks west towards Route N-7 and La Coucourde, running into Groupe Wilde (Clarke and Smith, ch. 9); Dahlquist had dissolved it as a separate entity on 23 August and reconstituted it on the 24th. Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 9, p. 162: "Task Force Butler, after a grueling night march, assembled in the Condillac Pass, ready to drive west toward the highway"; Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 9, p. 154: "On the morning of 23 August, Dahlquist dissolved Task Force Butler as a separate entity". Location: Condillac, Drôme (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the village of Condillac; the attack went from the western exit of the pass towards La Coucourde, about 3 km away. Location support: Clarke and Smith name the Condillac Pass. Commander: Brigadier General Frederick B. Butler, VI Corps deputy commander (Clarke and Smith, ch. 5).

current_activity: built round the 3rd Battalion, 157th Infantry, secures Loriol at the Drôme crossing
notes: Event date: 29 August 1944, afternoon (Clarke and Smith, ch. 9). Event definition: Repulsed at Loriol on 28 August, the task force, now built round the 3rd Battalion of the 157th Infantry, attacks again and secures Loriol in the afternoon of the 29th, but cannot push on to the Rhône (Clarke and Smith, ch. 9). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 9, p. 166: "despite stiff German opposition, Task Force Butler secured". Location: Loriol-sur-Drôme, Drôme (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Clarke and Smith name Loriol. Commander: Brigadier General Frederick B. Butler, VI Corps deputy commander (Clarke and Smith, ch. 5).
